Hi Olivia / Daniel —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can scope pricing and provide a hosted API quote. High-level items from our side: 

- Expected monthly token volume: ~150,000,000 tokens/month (they mentioned 120–180M as a range).
- Typical request profile: user messages average ~80 tokens, model response average ~120 tokens (~200 tokens per call).
- Peak TPS (calls): ~25 RPS during peak hourly windows; concurrency: ~200 concurrent requests at peak.
- Important for cost: they want target unit economics of roughly $8–$12 per 1M tokens for hosted API (they asked what a target $/1M looks like).

Action items for Olivia / Daniel: can you confirm the monthly range (low/high) and whether you expect significant burst windows >25 RPS? Also confirm any regulatory constraints (data residency) that affect routing.

Next steps: I'll loop in Rishi to run a quick estimate (attached usage sheet) and propose a hosted pricing band + short-term pilot plan. If the numbers look good we can schedule a 30-min pricing + SOW alignment call early next week.

Attachments: usage-estimate-v2.xlsx (filled by their SM), pricing-sheet-q1-2026.pdf (Redwood sample pricing band)

Thanks,

Thanks — looping in a few clarifying items from infra/SE so our estimate is accurate: 

- When you say ~30 RPS bursts, is that for sustained periods (>=30 minutes) or short spikes (~5–10 minutes)? Sustained bursts change provisioning.
- Do you expect caching or prefix reuse (we can often reduce billed tokens with prefix caching for system prompts / repeated context).
- Any SLA / latency SLO expectations for the pilot (p95 < 300ms for responses)?

I'll take the usage-estimate-v2.xlsx and run a cost model. Tentative hosted API band (ballpark) for 150M tokens/month is $8–$11 / 1M tokens depending on burst commitment and caching; with a 12-mo committed pilot we can likely move to $7.25–$9.25 / 1M. I'll put a modeled quote in the PDF and share a draft SOW.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min technical/pricing call Monday to go through the model.

Quick answers to Rishi's Qs: 

- Bursts: typically short spikes (~5–10 minutes) tied to marketing campaigns. Sustained >30 minutes is unlikely.
- Caching: we do some prefix reuse in chat flows (system prompt + product info), but expect most calls to be unique user input. Estimate effective cache savings ~8–12%.
- SLA: for the pilot, p95 < 500ms is acceptable; for full production we'd prefer p95 < 300ms.
